Results › Cell 000

Cell 000: n list, byte-aligned

The sorted list of every Carmichael number n. The first value is stored in full and each later value as its difference from the previous one, in a byte-aligned VByte code.

Switches: A off, B off, C off. What the switches mean.

Times are on an Intel Core i9-9900K (8 cores, 16 threads), 64 GB RAM, NVMe SSD, Windows 10. Decode times are in memory. The notes under the results table say how each time is measured.

Build

This file is not hosted. Rebuild it from the oracle with:

make fetch-oracle rebuild-000

The target first builds the n list (see intermediate files), then runs the encoder:

nstats_orc1 data/carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1 --emit-n work/n.raw --emit-only
list_build vbyte work/n.raw work/c000-n-vbyte.vbg

Verify, decode and certify

make verify-000
make fetch-oracle certify-000

Verify first checks the size and SHA-256 of the file. Then the targets run these commands:

# make verify-000
list_decode work/c000-n-vbyte.vbg
# make certify-000
list_decode work/c000-n-vbyte.vbg --kind n --certify data/carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1 --threads N
# make decode-000
list_decode work/c000-n-vbyte.vbg --emit work/c000.values.raw

N is the number of threads. The reproduce page explains the folders and the defaults.
